target_audience: University students with a basic interest in computer science and mathematics

sections.title: Prerequisite: The One-Way Street (Hashing)
lecture_lines: Cryptographic hashes create unique digital fingerprints.
The process is strictly a one-way street.
Input data is transformed into a fixed digest.
Reversing the operation is mathematically impossible.
Think of it as a permanent blender effect.
animations: Animate the blender creating a unique 'Smoothie' (hash) (#00FF00).
Show the smoothie cannot return to strawberry (#FF0000).

sections.title: The Digital Puzzle: Proof of Work
lecture_lines: Proof of Work validates network activity.
Miners guess nonces for specific hash results.
This trial and error requires immense effort.
animations: Display a large with a combination dial (#FFD700).
Animate successful guess triggering the to open (#00FF00).

sections.title: Chaining the Blocks
lecture_lines: Blocks chain together via previous hashes.
This creates an immutable chronological history.
Altering one link invalidates the entire chain.
animations: Draw arrows from each to the next (#FFFFFF).
Show a 'Breaking' animation on one invalidating the chain (#FF0000).

sections.title: Ownership: Elliptic Curve Cryptography
lecture_lines: Elliptic curve cryptography secures user ownership.
Private keys sign, public keys verify identity.
Deriving private keys is computationally infeasible.
animations: Display a 'Private Key' document icon (#FFD700) using.
Show a 'Public Sensor' verifying the signature (#00BFFF) using.
Animate the 'Public Key' derivation from the private key (#00FF00).

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
lecture_lines: Hashing, Proof-of-Work, and ECC form Bitcoin.
These primitives enable decentralized trust systems.
The network acts as a global ledger.
animations: Animate all components merging into a single 'Trust' icon (#00FF00).
